How Internet Culture and Franchise Twists Shaped This Year's Horror Films

The Box Office Strength of Horror

Horror cinema is enjoying another banner year, fueled by dedicated fans who consume media voraciously and treat theatrical viewings as communal events. According to horror critic and director Rebekah McKendry in an interview with NPR, the genre continues to thrive in theaters while other film categories struggle. Going to see a scary movie opening weekend with friends remains a reliable draw, keeping theatrical horror vibrant and relevant.

Internet-Born Concepts and Subverted Franchises

Discussions highlighting the year's top-performing horror releases point to two distinct thematic trends. First, internet culture has birthed major silver-screen concepts. For instance, "Backrooms" successfully transitioned from a viral internet phenomenon into one of the year's top-performing films. Similarly, "Iron Lung" leveraged digital reach, having been adapted from a video game and produced by YouTuber Markiplier.

Second, long-running franchises are actively subverting traditional formulas. Films like "28 Years Later: The Bone Temple" introduce vastly different characters and unexpected narrative directions compared to their predecessors. On television, established properties such as "Carrie," "IT," and "Crystal Lake" continue to find new life.

Dark comedy horrors have also risen to prominence, combining sharp social commentary with absurdist humor. Titles like "Obsession" and Casper Kelly's "Buddy," alongside the TV horror-comedy series "Widow's Bay," demonstrate how effectively the genre can blend laughs with scares.

Accessible Recommendations for Spooky Season

For viewers seeking Halloween-appropriate viewing without excessive gore or jump scares, McKendry recommends two lower-profile titles. "Undertone" follows a podcaster examining unsettling sound files without relying on graphic monster reveals. Additionally, the Netflix mini-series "Below" anchors its sea-monster narrative within a grounded community family drama.

Practical Implications and Verification

Readers interested in exploring these titles can verify release details, trailers, and streaming availability directly through official distribution platforms or review the original discussion via [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/27/nx-s1-6007893/how-internet-culture-and-franchise-twists-defined-this-years-horror-movies). While critics highlight general trends like internet adaptation and franchise pivots, individual viewer reactions to tone, humor, and intensity will vary.
